Sub-issue: Applying for or obtaining a modification, forbearance plan, short sale, or deed-in-lieu
Consumer complaint narrative:
I inherited this home when my mom passed away last year, and I had a lot of trouble being confirmed as successor in interest to even get information about the mortgage. It took Shellpoint Mortgage Servicing months to confirm me, and after Id sent them the information they requested many times, they finally confirmed me as SII but didnt tell me on one of the many phone calls I had with them during this time. They foreclosed on the house, and sold it at auction, after I was confirmed as SII, without giving me the chance to apply for a modification, or giving me the same rights as the original owner. I filed a complaint on here, and was one day away from being evicted from my home, when I received an email from them that they reviewed my complaint and decided to rescind the sale. I was ecstatic after the emotional turmoil Id been through from the eviction process, and from being one day away from being homeless. I thought Id finally be given the same rights as the original owner, and be able to modify the loan, and apply for the XXXX Mortgage Assistance Program to catch up the past due payments. But when I spoke to my point of contact, XXXX XXXX at Shellpoint, she informed me I couldnt apply for a modification because the loan wasnt in my name, and I couldnt have it transferred into my name, because the loan was past due. She told me I would need to apply for a loan assumption and I would need to have enough income and credit to be considered, but I wouldnt be approved because the loan was already past due. I was not offered any loss mitigation options because she said since the loan wasnt in my name, it wouldnt be approved. I told her thats not what the mortgage servicing rules from the CFPB state, and I quoted her this from their website : - [ ] Under 1024.30 ( d ), a confirmed successor in interest must be considered a borrower for purposes of this subpart and 1024.17, regardless of whether the successor in interest assumes the mortgage loan obligation under State law. For example, if a servicer receives a loss mitigation application from a confirmed successor in interest, the servicer must review and evaluate the application and notify the confirmed successor in interest in accordance with the procedures set forth in 1024.41 if the property is the confirmed successor in interest 's principal residence and the procedures set forth in 1024.41 are otherwise applicable. Treatment of a confirmed successor in interest as a borrower for purposes of this subpart and 1024.17 does not affect whether the confirmed successor in interest is subject to the contractual obligations of the mortgage loan agreement, which is determined by applicable State law.

Also this rule about having the loan put into my name : - [ ] Todays interpretive rule explains that because an heir has already acquired the title to the home, adding the heir as a borrower on the mortgage does not trigger the Ability-to-Repay requirements. The rule does not require the creditor to determine the heirs ability to repay the mortgage before formally recognizing the heir as the borrower. As the named borrower, the heir may more easily be able to obtain account information, pay off the loan, or seek a loan modification.

But she didnt agree with that and neither did anyone above her. I spoke with a few different supervisors throughout this ordeal and none of them agreed this. They all told me I couldnt assume the loan or do a transfer of ownership, or any kind of loss mitigation without proving my income and doing a credit check. I applied for the XXXX Mortgage Assistance Program, and they were going to approve me but they needed the loan to be in my name. They wouldve paid the entire loan off because there was only {$42000.00} left to pay on it, and they provide up to {$50000.00} worth of assistance. So I researched the rules with the CFPB, and with XXXX XXXX, who I was told owned the mortgage, on transfers of ownership so I could have it in my name. I called Shellpoint and asked to have the loan transferred into my name, but was told I couldnt do that by two different supervisors. They told me again Id have to apply for a mortgage assumption, and have the credit and income to be approved. I quoted them the rules from XXXX XXXX website on transfers of ownership and the federal restrictions on the exercise of the due on transfer clause : Permitted Transfers of Ownership subject to conditions In situations where all of the following conditions are met, XXXX XXXX will permit a Transfer of Ownership of the Mortgaged Premises : At least 12 months have passed since the Origination Date The Servicer has complied with all mortgage insurance requirements applicable to the transfer Either The transfer is to a transferee who occupies or will occupy the Mortgaged Premises as a Primary Residence and is : A parent or child of the transferor, or A grandparent or grandchild of the transferor, or A brother or sister of the transferor, or An original co-Borrower of the transferor under the Note, whether or not related to the transferor In connection with any Transfer of Ownership that meets the conditions of this Section 8406.4, a Servicer may not evaluate the creditworthiness of a transferee, require a transferee to assume the Mortgage or otherwise require the Servicers or XXXX XXXX approval of the transfer.

I was still told I couldnt do a transfer of ownership without doing a full assumption and evaluation of my creditworthiness, even after quoting them all of the above information. I spoke with a few different supervisors, and they told me I was interpreting it the wrong way. I explained that I just wanted to do a transfer or ownership so I could get approved for Georgia Mortgage Assistance program, and have the remaining loan paid off. The GMA program had to have something with my name on it in order to approve me. Even though I was approved as SII with Shellpoint, my name wasnt on any documents with them. They had everything under The estate of XXXX XXXX who is my mother, and the original borrower. Shellpoint told me there was no way to have my name on the loan without doing a complete assumption. Even after reading them the guidelines from the XXXX XXXX website, none of them would do a transfer of ownership for me, so that I could have my name on the loan, and get approved for GMA program, and have the loan paid off. The supervisors at Shellpoint argued with me and said that they dont do transfers of ownership and that I wasnt understanding the XXXX XXXX guidelines or the mortgage servicing rules the correct way. So even after the first foreclosure sale was rescinded, I still wasnt given the same rights as the original borrower, or given any loss mitigation options, and I couldnt have the loan put into my name, so that I could get any foreclosure relief assistance. Even though the rules from the CFPB explicitly state theyre supposed to do all of those things. The loan was too far past due for me to catch up on my own, but I wouldve been approved for the Georgia Mortgage Assistance program, who wouldve paid off the remaining {$42000.00} owed on it, if the loan was in my name. Shellpoint wouldnt allow me to do a transfer of ownership or follow any of the rules theyre required to follow when someone inherits a home after the death of a loved one. My mother left me her home when she passed away, and the CFPB made rules for this exact situation, and to make it an easy process. But I still dont own the home. Im going to have to go through the eviction process again, and face being homeless with my son once again.

I called back in 72 hours, and was then told, we can not process this because we need the digits on your card ( which I did not bring to XXXX but had booked using my online account that I could log into ). This Amex associate told me enjoy my trip, call when back and they'd process the application of points as it should have done at checkout.

I called when home and spoke to three different departments, the first one transferring me to the second to complete, and second to a third that could do it, and the third department telling me, sorry it is already processed and we can not switch it over to your points on your Everyday Card. No logical explanation back was given to me. I then filed a dispute with the card, and was told to call them for a resolution. I called back on XX/XX/XXXX and spent 38 minutes, being told until the last minute that he was going to apply the points to the charge with no problem. At the end he said no, sorry can not transfer the points to apply to the charge made on your Gold Card. I reiterated again that I did not charge this to my Gold Card, I had logged into the Rewards website for my Everyday Card ( which had the XXXX points ) and had only authorized my Gold Card to pay the excess fees and taxes. He said sorry, the system won't let me do it. Fourth, I called immediately and was hesitant to stay at the hotel unless I could use points and offered to cancel, but was reassured by the agent over and over, that I would be able to apply the points in 72 hours. Fifth, I called American Express multiple times ( probably spending 4 hours total ) on the lines with various representatives, to be mislead that it would be ok and they could fix it, and then at the end, they would say sorry the system will not do it, we can not help you.

Consumer complaint narrative:
Today, on XX/XX/XXXX I accessed my online account to pay my credit card balance and I noticed a recent charge, which stood out to me since I haven't utilized the card for weeks while self-quarantining for Covid-19. It was a " Rewards Annual Membership Fee. '' I didn't recognize this charge so I tried to access the information about where it came from, but no details were provided on the link -- which is not typical. Most vendors provide a phone number at the very minimum. Suspecting fraud I called card services right away. When I asked the representative to find me a contact number for that entity he laughed and said that it was Wells Fargo. This was the first time I heard of any Rewards associated with this credit card. This representative told me that he had to 'erase ' all of the points that he said I had earned ( apparently 13K+ ), stating that it was the only way that he could proceed in resolving this dispute as he couldn't get past that window without me agreeing to let him delete the points. I told him that I was fine with that so long as all charges, current and past, were credited back to me. I then asked him to go back and see how many times over the past several years I had been charged. After waiting on hold he returned to the line and said that there had been no previous charges. By this point I had started going through my tax files and found statements from XXXX and XXXX, each showing a {$50.00} awards membership charge. He then transferred me to someone in " customer care. '' This person started the conversation by saying that I had accessed my rewards. I informed her that this was definitely not the case as I had no knowledge of said rewards until today and that the only person who accessed them was the representative I had first spoken to who deleted all of the points. 

I spent an hour and a half trying to get this issue resolved. At the time that I opened this account there was no mention of any rewards program or any annual fee associated with this account. It may have been hidden somewhere in the fine print, but I guarantee you that as part of the conversation with the banker I would have insisted on reassurance that there were no annual fees associated with the card. This credit card was going to be dedicated to a small business with low volume purchases ( low reward opportunity ) and I would NEVER have agreed to pay an annual fee -- nor would I have failed to ask if there was an annual fee for the card. I have great credit and I can obtain a credit card from any company that I want -- I would NOT have agreed to a fee. I'm submitting this complaint because it seems reasonable to assume that I'm not the only person who has experienced this problem. All in all it appears that at the very minimum they've fraudulently charged my account {$200.00}. I am insisting on FULL reimbursement for every charge, seeing as I've never accessed said rewards and had no knowledge until today of said rewards. I'm told that my case ( # XXXX ) has been moved up to " Case Management '' at Wells Fargo. They gave me a direct access number of XXXX. Though I have been verbally assured that the most recent charge of {$50.00} has been removed, there is not evidence of this credit on my online account as of yet.
Company public response: Company has responded to the consumer and the CFPB and chooses not to provide a public response

Review of Policies : Conduct an internal review of overdraft and charged-off account handling policies to ensure transparency and better communication. 

Compensation : Provide compensation for the financial and emotional distress caused by this incident. 

Conclusion : This experience has undermined my trust in Citizens Banks ability to safeguard my funds and provide reliable customer service. It is imperative that corrective action is taken promptly to address this issue and prevent similar occurrences for other customers.

Sub-issue: Funds not handled or disbursed as instructed
Consumer complaint narrative:
I am filing a formal complaint against U.S. Bank for failure to honor a business checking promotional bonus. Despite meeting all written requirements, the bank is attempting to deny the bonus by enforcing " hidden '' restrictions not found in the original disclosure. 

Facts of Compliance : Requirement A ( Balance ) : I deposited and maintained over {$25000.00}, satisfying the " New Money '' requirement within the 30-day window and maintained it for 60 days.

Requirement B ( Transactions ) : I completed 5 qualifying transactions. U.S. Banks disclosure explicitly defines " ACH credits '' as a qualifying transaction type. My records show 5 distinct ACH credits totaling over {$25000.00}. 

The Dispute ( Case # XXXX ) : On XX/XX/year>, I contacted customer service. The agent ( XXXX XXXX stated : " Making the deposits is the first requirement and therefore can not also be the second requirement. '' The bank claims that because the ACH credits were used to fund the account ( Requirement A ), they are disqualified from counting toward the 5 transactions ( Requirement B ).

Legal Violation : The written terms do not state that deposits used for the balance requirement are excluded from the transaction count. By adding this " mutually exclusive '' rule after the fact, the bank is in breach of its own disclosure. Any ambiguity in the term " also '' must be interpreted in favor of the consumer under the principle of Contra Proferentem. I have attached the chat transcript where the agent admits to this arbitrary interpretation. 

Furthermore, subsequent interactions with different agents provided conflicting and inconsistent justifications for the denial. One agent claimed the issue was the word 'also, ' while another later claimed that 'funding deposits ' are categorically excluded from being qualifying transactions. This inconsistency demonstrates that the bank is arbitrarily creating new barriers to entry that are not present in the written terms. It appears the bank is exercising unfettered 'discretionary interpretation ' to avoid paying promised bonuses, which creates an impossible and deceptive standard for consumers to follow.

From XXXX through XXXX {$110.00} of the {$750.00} was added each month to my account. In nine months I had only {$850.00} available for debt negotiations after paying {$6500.00}. In those nine months {$5900.00} were paid as fees. The first negotiation and payment to a creditor occurred in XXXX. Payment was issued on XX/XX/XXXX and sent by overnight delivery. 

Obviously, the entity that benefited most was the debt settlement company. These upfront payments are illegal breaking the TSR laws. Many of these companies have stated that they are exempt. However, over and over the courts have found that they are not exempt and held them responsible. Payment processing companies like Global Client Solutions have been found responsible for releasing these payments knowing that upfront fees are illegal, even though they act as if they dont know that they are illegal. They also have knowledge when creditors have begun receiving payment since they are the ones issuing the payments. 

Global is already known to the CFPB who filed a case against them and their chief executives, XXXX and XXXX. A Stipulated Consent order was entered into for {>= $1,000,000} in redress penalties to CFPB as well as another {>= $1,000,000} in civil penalties to CFPB. Lengthy rules dealing with policy expectations, vetting of business affiliations, reporting to CFPB and monitoring by CFPB were involved. This occurred in XX/XX/XXXX. 

Global has disregarded all of the rules that they agreed to follow in the Consent Order, as my simple math illustrates. Global releases the payments. Their responsibility should be to the consumers who own the accounts. They need to follow the law and not make fee payments until the legal requirements are met. The law states that no advanced fees can be made until : 1.settlement negotiations are reached with the creditor ; 2.the settlement is agreed to by the customer ; and 3.at least one payment has been made to the creditor. 

As I stated previously, the first payment was made on XX/XX/XXXX by overnight delivery. You can view all of the payment activity on the attached record of my dedicated account with Global Client Solutions, beginning XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX when I closed my account. 

Their accounting can be difficult to follow : - A Retainer Fee of {$150.00} for two months, then {$100.00} for six months ; - An Administration Fee of {$89.00} for every month you are in the program ; and - A Service Fee of {$430.00}, which is 17 % of the entire debt enrolled in the program divided into 22 monthly payments. 
These fees should not have been released until the program had completed the negotiation with each creditor. Only when negotiations are completed for each debt, can fees for each debt be released. 

Global has blatantly disregarded the enforcement the CFPB enacted in XXXX. I am hopeful that there are ways to be sure that these payment processing organizations can be taught that complicity in breaking the law and setting customers up for failure is unacceptable and punishable. 


Thank you very much for your attention to this matter, XXXX XXXX

On XX/XX/XXXX, I made a payment to CitiBank to pay off the remaining balance on my balance transfer offer in the amount of {$2400.00} that is due on XX/XX/XXXX. The payment was not allocated to the balance transfer to pay it off ; it was allocated to the highest interest-bearing amount, then to the balance transfer payoff, which would not completely payoff my balance transfer by the due date of XX/XX/XXXX resulting in interest being charged to the remaining balance of my balance transfer. 

I spoke with CitiBank on XX/XX/XXXX, to ensure the payment I submitted in the amount of {$2400.00} would be allocated to pay off my balance transfer that was expiring on XX/XX/XXXX. I first spoke with XXXX, who was very helpful in letting me know she could not help and would need to transfer me to a supervisor. The supervisor I spoke with also could not reallocate my payment, so I was transferred to his supervisor, XXXX. XXXX was less than helpful in stating no CitiBank employee could process a reallocation of my payment. A referral was to be submitted, but they could not guarantee the allocation would take place to pay off my balance transfer in the amount of {$2400.00}. I asked to speak with XXXX 's supervisor, and she advised me she was the supervisor for account services, and I would need to contact the corporate office, which she offered to provide me with the address, as well as letting me know that no one at the corporate office has the ability to reallocate the payment I made and it would take 15 or more business days for the corporate office to get back to me.

Sub-issue: Trying to communicate with the company to fix an issue related to modification, forbearance, short sale, deed-in-lieu, bankruptcy, or foreclosure
Consumer complaint narrative:
I inherited my late fathers home in XXXX and have issues with NewRez and Shellpoint since. 

They continued to advise they needed additional documentation from probate proving I am the sole heir, and when I provided the documentation I thought they needed ( several times, over multiple months ) they refused to advise that the documentation was not what they were asking for or would flat out tell me Im not sure it goes to a different department. 

We fell upon financial struggle that put us behind and an impending foreclosure date was provided earlier this year. I worked with someone who helped put the loan in forbearance, and advised I could then apply for a repayment plan or a modification. Once the two month forbearance was over, she reached out to gain additional information to move forward with an application for the modification. I provided all necessary information, and was not advised I was missing anything until I CCd her on an email to the loss mitigation department with the full list of documents requested. She then emailed me and advised she was no longer my point of contact and to call the XXXX number to reapply and be reappointed a new single point of contact. 

There was no further explanation, so I called and reapplied. Still, I was not advised that I had been denied for the modification, nor why ( that one document was missing and I didnt realize ). I was told 5-7 business days to be assigned a POC, and nothing could be done until I was contacted by that POC. I waited 5 business days days, called, and was advised that there was no updates yet. I called again the following Monday to be told that I was not eligible as I did not provide the correct documentation. Instead of reaching out to let me know so that I could make the easy fix needed, they waited for me to reach out despite that I was advised the opposite. 

In the last year I have called and discussed my options at least 20+ times with someone over the phone, as well as daily/ weekly communication via email. This entire time I was under the impression that we were working toward a loan modification application, when in reality they were giving me the run around and I feel as if this was their intention all along. 

I have received little to no advice, education, etc from the company, and in turn believe they are unlawfully stalling to force foreclosure ( which is coming up in a week ).

Freedom Mortage Coorporation.

I am requesting : 1. A final written determination of all loss mitigation options available.

2. A halt to all foreclosure activity while my application is under review.

3. Assignment of a single point of contact for all communications regarding my loan.

This cycle has caused financial and emotional hardship, and I believe the servicer is violating federal law. 
As we are also under an active lawsuit regarding the property as well due to undisclosed fire damage.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I have been a Wells Fargo customer for over 30 years and have a checking and savings account enrolled in the " Save As You Go '' transfer program. This program was advertised as a way to waive the monthly service fee. However, despite meeting the stated requirements, I was charged a monthly service fee on multiple occasions. 

When I contacted Wells Fargo for an explanation, I received misleading and conflicting information from multiple representatives. One falsely claimed I must have changed my transfer settings, which I did not. Another told me there was an additional requirement to make debit purchases or bill payments, which was never disclosed when I enrolled in the program.

I asked for official documentation proving these requirements, but the representatives struggled to find it. One representative provided me with a separate URL buried within my monthly statement PDF, claiming it contained the relevant terms. However, when I copied and pasted the link, there was no mention of 'Save As You Go ' anywhere on that page. Additionally, I was directed to a FAQ link titled " What fees other than monthly service fees are calculated monthly for my consumer account? " which is misleading because I was specifically seeking information about monthly service fees. 

When I asked for proof of when and how I was notified of this requirement ( email or mail ), they placed me on hold for over 20 minutes and could not provide a clear answer.

After 2.5 hours on the phone and multiple escalations, I was told they could only file a complaint and could not immediately refund the improper fees. 

Requested Resolution : A full refund of all improperly charged service fees. 
A written explanation of the current 'Save As You Go ' terms and all requirements to waive monthly fees.

A review of Wells Fargos disclosure practices to ensure this information is clearly provided to customers. 
This appears to be an unfair and deceptive fee practice, and I urge the CFPB to investigate.

Issue: Problem caused by your funds being low
Consumer complaint narrative:
Our accounts were opened in XXXX of XXXX at a Wells Fargo Branch in XXXX PA. The accounts we opened were a checking account and a savings account and the savings account would be accessed if the checking account was overdrawn and we would be charged a {$12.00} fee for these overdrafts. These accounts were maintained until XX/XX/XXXX when Wells Fargo arbitrarily closed the savings account. This action resulted in an increase to {$35.00} for each overdraft transaction. 
What we are disputing today is : why Wells Fargo closed the savings account resulting in us paying higher fees than we would have been charged if the account remained open. 
This complaint is also being filed because of the fees currently being charged to the checking account that is still open. For this checking account we access the account information through a Wells Fargo banking app which we check to ensure that the balance in the account is sufficient to cover pending and future transactions. Even though Wells Fargos mobile app would consistently show we had sufficient funds to cover pending and anticipated transactions, when these transactions were processed by Wells Fargo the result was us being charged overdraft fees to the checking account. 
This activity occurred over an extended period of time which led to a visit by us to a local Wells Fargo branch to get an explanation as to what was causing the fees to be charged when the mobile app showed sufficient funds to cover these transactions. No explanation was provided at that time as the branch associate could not explain why the fees were being charged. The fees were reversed that day, however, the next day additional fees were charged against the account. We returned to the branch with the same questions and the manager called another area of Wells Fargo for an explanation. The manager was told that the information in the mobile app did not reflect current information and was inconsistent with internal account information. 
Following that inquiry, Wells Fargo began to charge us NSF fees on top of the overdraft fees as well. Based on what has occurred with this account we believe 1 ; Wells Fargo purposely closed the savings account in order to charge higher fees for overdrafts and 2 ; Wells Fargo knew the information in their mobile app did not match their internal information and intentionally used that knowledge to charge additional fees as well. 
These deceptive actions by Wells Fargo has cost us thousands of dollars in fees which we believe should be refunded to us. We believe, Wells Fargos arbitrary actions to close our savings account was done to charge us higher fees. We also believe, Wells Fargo was also aware of the inconsistency of the information in their mobile app and internal account information but continued to charge us fees based on this inconsistency of information. 
After numerous attempts to resolve these issues with Wells Fargo we are writing this complaint with the hope that these practices would be investigated and brought to light and that the fees charged would be refunded to us. Attached you would find records of fee activity showing fees charged.

Citi applies payments above the minimum to high-interest balances first, meaning my fixed autopay amount was no longer being applied fully to the promotional balance. Allow me to cancel or reverse the deposit so I may re-deposit the check at another institution.

If not corrected, I believe this hold policy represents a pattern of unfair and deceptive banking practices under the CFPBs UDAAP authority ( 12 U.S.C. 5531 ) and a violation of the Expedited Funds Availability Act.

Supporting Documentation : I have attached the deposit hold notice email from BMO dated XX/XX/year> confirming the hold amount, deposit date, and release timeline.
